The STT wrapper fixtures execute unchanged methods and helpers from `ezlocalai/STT.py` in reference revision `0f7e9f45ac0d67ea806ee19874f98bb8f47c7544`. Its SHA-256 is `d0dd8340c243d7ff9ba84f4e3babe3c41b0b0ce7c7dddf2565eb886ba3f21fe2`. AST extraction excludes imports and unrelated listening/diarization methods without rewriting the captured method bodies. Repository implementations and runners are C++.

`../stt_runtime_cases.jsonl` contains 800 source cases: 240 initialization/close cases and 560 transcription cases with subsequent calls. Model factories/inference, CUDA/cuDNN/audio operations, filesystem operations, UUIDs and diarization are substituted at their boundaries. Captures compare outputs and exception categories/messages, device/compute/handle state, remaining files, weak-reference model residency at collection points, and dependency-call order. They include CPU thread selection, the 1,000 MB GPU threshold, cuDNN probe failures, constructor and inference CPU fallback, failed reloads, repeated close, calls after close, legacy batch aliasing, raw granularity/temperature values, whitespace/word filtering, language fallback, diarized formatting and cleanup-error precedence. Failure paths deliberately retain files where the source does. The external generator is `/tmp/ezlocalai_stt_runtime_oracle.py`.

`../stt_runtime_io_cases.jsonl` adds nine cases using real Linux filesystem operations in both the unchanged reference wrapper and the C++ test: normal cleanup, missing outputs, a regular file as the outputs directory, a directory at the target, a symlink to `/dev/full`, a dangling symlink, replacement of the audio file by a directory during inference, a NUL in the extension and invalid base64. Tests compare exception categories/messages and the remaining file type. Buffered write/close errors omit the filename, while open/unlink errors include it; cleanup must leave an unexpected directory in place. Temporary root paths are normalized to `/work`. Inference and microphone initialization are substituted, and CUDA is unavailable. The external generator is `/tmp/ezlocalai_stt_runtime_io_oracle.py`.

`../stt_runtime_model_{modern,legacy}.jsonl` contains 15 actual-model calls per profile. These execute the same unchanged wrapper methods with real faster-whisper 1.2.0/1.0.3, CTranslate2 4.6.1, tokenizers 0.22.1, NumPy 1.26.4, PyAV 12.3.0 and ONNX Runtime 1.24.1. CUDA availability is false; PyAudio 0.2.14 initializes and terminates real PortAudio. Inference, base64 decoding, file writes/removal, audio decoding, VAD, feature extraction, tokenization, standard/batched transcription and wrapper formatting run normally. Native tests use four inference threads, one OpenBLAS thread, substituted GPU availability and default native PortAudio operations. CPU-thread selection itself is tested separately in the policy fixtures. Separate audio error/lifetime comparisons are documented in `../stt_audio_README.md`.

Cases cover English and multilingual tiny models, prompt/beam settings, translation, automatic language detection, word timestamps, long audio, standard and batched requests, silence/empty WAV, invalid audio and zero batch size. The legacy profile rejects `batch_size` when its batch alias calls the standard model; that error is preserved. Tests compare exact output text and JSON (timestamps allow 1e-12 binary-arithmetic differences), exception category/message, real temporary-file cleanup, and explicit close behavior. Model/configuration/tokenizer/vocabulary identities match the pinned models documented in `../whisper_transcription_assets/README.md`. Metadata records every audio SHA-256, dependency profile and thread setting; tests also verify the VAD identities.

The WAV files are signed 16-bit mono/16 kHz renditions of the public JFK samples and zero-sample/silence inputs documented in `../whisper_transcription_assets/README.md`. `invalid.bin` contains generated non-audio text. The source generator is `/tmp/ezlocalai_stt_runtime_model_oracle.py`. Its audio files are shared by the two profiles; run profile captures sequentially if recreating these assets.

The real-model runner now uses the native resolver with local directories and offline alias snapshots containing the same verified model files, plus native PortAudio initialization. GPU availability remains substituted. Model acquisition has separate HTTP/cache fixtures documented in `../hub_snapshot_README.md`; these inference fixtures do not establish network transport behavior. GPU/platform behavior, recording streams/device selection, service pool/API integration, native speaker diarization, arbitrary raw invalid backend options, codecs and corrupted model configurations remain outside this coverage.

The separate `../stt_runtime_model_modern_gpu.jsonl` adds the same 15 modern-profile
calls using real Torch 2.9.1+cu128 GPU selection and float16 CTranslate2 inference.
It uses the same verified assets. Both native and source runs assert that their
models stay on CUDA after every call; the existing 30 CPU cases remain separate.
The optional native GPU test includes explicit close and file cleanup. Platform
captures, dependencies, hardware identity and remaining GPU limitations are
documented in `../stt_torch_README.md`.
